Series::masked_scatter_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::masked_scatter_(const Series& mask, const Series& src) const -> Series&

What It Does¶

masked_scatter_() performs the same sequential mask-driven write as masked_scatter(), but it writes directly into the current Series and returns the same handle.

Use it when the masked write itself is the state change you want to keep.

Parameters¶

The parameters are the same as masked_scatter():

  • mask must be boolean and may broadcast to the current destination shape

  • src.numel() must equal the number of true positions in the broadcasted mask

Returns¶

Series& The same Series, after mutation.

Examples¶

Example 1. A basic in-place masked scatter updates only the true positions.

auto base = pluss::make_series({10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0});
auto mask = pluss::make_series({true, false, true, false}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool);
auto src = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});

base.masked_scatter_(mask, src);
std::cout << base;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 20, 2, 40]

Example 2. Broadcasted masks work on the in-place form too.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 20.0, 30.0},
    {40.0, 50.0, 60.0},
});
auto column_mask = pluss::make_series({true, false, true}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool);
auto src = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0});

matrix.masked_scatter_(column_mask, src);
std::cout << matrix;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 20, 2],
  [3, 50, 4]]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • This method mutates the current value.

  • Source values are consumed sequentially in logical mask order.

  • The same boolean-mask and source-count rules from masked_scatter() still apply.

Summary¶

Use masked_scatter_() when boolean-mask-driven writes should land directly on the current Series.

See Also¶

  • Series::masked_scatter: the out-of-place sibling.

  • Series::scatter_: in-place indexed writes by integer positions instead of a mask.
